action_items.item: Add a regression test for monthly_statement.py that covers an account with no data, so the max() call on an empty iterable is caught before release.
Tie flag rollouts to error-rate monitoring. Roll the flag out in stages, and automatically pause or roll back the flag if the account page error rate rises.
Require an empty-data test case to pass before monthly-spend-feature, or any similar flag, can be switched on in production.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers saw account page requests fail. The error rate went from {errors_before} to {errors_while_broken} on average and peaked at {errors_at_worst}, and the HighErrorRate alert fired.
The failing requests raised ValueError: max() iterable argument is empty at monthly_statement.py:626, starting in the same minute the incident began.

The monthly statement code path only ran when monthly-spend-feature evaluated on. The flag went from off to on and was evaluated on for a growing share of requests. At 08:07 it was on for 38 of 200 evaluations, and by 08:08 it was on for every sampled evaluation.

The code behind the flag does not handle an empty iterable, so every request that reached that line with no data raised an error. Production changes showed no deploy, so the flag change was the trigger. Turning the flag off ended the errors.

contributing_factors.factor: The flag's code path was enabled for a growing share of live traffic without having been shown to handle empty data. The fix is only a draft pull request and is not yet merged.
Nothing checked the error rate while the flag rollout was in progress, so the flag stayed on until the HighErrorRate alert fired. That alert came several minutes after the errors began.
No test covers the empty-iterable case in the monthly statement code, so the bug reached production.

input.executive_summary: For {duration}, from {began} until {recovered}, a share of shopper requests to the account pages of io-shop failed. The error rate rose from {errors_before} to an average of {errors_while_broken} and peaked at {errors_at_worst}. A feature flag had been turned on, and the code it enabled crashed on some accounts. Argus switched the flag back off, and the error rate returned to baseline. A draft pull request with a code fix is open for review.

got_lucky: The failure affected only some requests, since the code path crashes only on empty data, and a flag revert was enough to stop it. A failure on every request, or one that a revert could not undo, would have been worse.
went_well: Argus ranked the flag change as the leading cause within seconds and reverted it, and the service was confirmed back at baseline.
The error log line gave the exact file and line, which tied the failure to the flag path.
The flag history showed the change even though there was no production deploy.
went_wrong: The flag was switched on with no check that its code path handles empty data.
The alert fired several minutes after the errors began, so shoppers were affected before anyone responded.

input.root_cause: The monthly-spend-feature flag was switched on for a growing share of requests, which enabled a code path in monthly_statement.py:626 that calls max() on an empty iterable and raises a ValueError, so account page requests failed.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for some shoppers
